notes: 🕳 The Gap Report now carries its own ten-year verdict. We backtested every gap in the ten-year store (247,775 gap days, 39 million rows, buys lagged one day so every trade was placeable): no gap group beat simply holding the market's quiet shares after costs, and every gap group won LESS often (38–43% of the time vs 47%). Surprises: faded up-gaps did BEST in the following week and held ones worst — and a down-gap that bounced back during the day was the weakest group of all. So the section labels now describe the day without predicting anything (“buyers stayed” rather than “strength”), and the finding is printed at the top of the report. The Gap Report stays — as a lens on what happened, not a reason to buy.
